integrity: The proof starts from an isolated selected vertex. In a crown graph this confines all selected vertices on the opposite side to its unique nonneighbor. If that nonneighbor is absent, domination forces the entire original bipartition class. If it is present, forced defender swaps lead to a selected set with no isolated vertex, contradicting isolate security. This yields exactly the two bipartition classes. The direct checker independently tests every subset for n=3 through 7.
scientific_limitations: The all-set classification is stated for crown graphs Cr_n with n at least four; Cr_3 has fourteen isolate secure dominating sets.
The result treats deletion of one perfect matching from K_{n,n}, not arbitrary edge deletions.
Finite enumeration covers n from three through seven and is corroborative rather than the proof for arbitrary n.
A differently phrased or non-indexed treatment of the same crown family may exist.
title: Isolate secure domination of crown graphs
